# Audit: Silent Exception-Swallow Patterns — legacy/Global module

*Read-only audit, 2026-07-05. Same method as `docs/AUDIT_Billing_exceptions.md`; scope here is the Global module, which the whole-codebase pattern audit (`docs/AUDIT_WholeCodebase_patterns.md`) flagged at ~7,545 empty-catch findings via a plain grep count but did not classify further. This audit reproduces that count with the same full classification rigor used for Billing (severity, exception type, billing-critical vs. peripheral) rather than a single grep tally.*

**Scope:** every `.java` file under `legacy/Global` (2669 files, 10511 parsed catch blocks).

**Method:** read-only. Automated structural parse (comment/string-aware brace matching) of every `catch` block, classified by body content, cross-checked by manual sampling (spot-checked ~10 findings and exclusions directly against source; all matched their classification). No file under `legacy/` was modified.

**Definition used (per task, identical to the Billing audit):** a finding is any catch block that is (a) empty, (b) returns `null`/a generic hardcoded error with no logging of the real cause, or (c) neither logs (via a real logger call) nor rethrows. Catch blocks that call a logger (`logger.error(...)`, etc.) or that `throw`/rethrow are excluded as non-findings.

## Summary

- **Total catch blocks parsed:** 10511
- **Total findings (silent-swallow pattern matches):** 9000
- **Non-findings:** 1456 properly rethrow (`throw`); 55 properly log via a real logger call
- **By severity:** silent-swallow = 8671, status-masks-failure = 37, other = 292
- **By path:** billing-critical = 960, peripheral = 8040

| Severity | Billing-critical | Peripheral |
|---|---|---|
| status-masks-failure | 14 | 23 |
| silent-swallow | 879 | 7792 |
| other | 67 | 225 |

**Only 15 of 2669 files (0.6%) import any real logging library** (`org.apache.log4j.Logger` or `org.slf4j.Logger`). The other 2654 files have no logger at all, so any non-rethrowing catch in them is structurally silent by construction — same structural finding as the Billing audit (28/558, 5%), now confirmed at a similar or worse rate in Global.

## Methodology caveats (read before acting on this list)

- **billing-critical vs peripheral is a path/filename/import heuristic**, not a data-flow analysis. A Global file is marked billing-critical if: (a) it lives under a `com/param/billing/` or `com/param/global/billing/` package; (b) its path/filename contains a payment/invoice/tariff/discount/deposit/fund/insurance/razorpay/pesapal/charge/voucher/refund/bill/consumption/collection/sanction/mpesa/ccavenue keyword; (c) it is `BillingExceptionController.java` (the shared centralized billing exception handler, explicitly named in scope); or (d) it is one of the 246 distinct Global classes directly imported anywhere in the `legacy/Billing` module (cross-checked via `grep` of every `import com.param.global.*` line across all of Billing). Everything else (OPD/encounter/appointment scheduling, patient master data, unit/organization config, mail/SMS utilities, DTOs, common utils not billing-specific) is marked peripheral. Borderline cases should be re-checked by whoever picks this up — e.g. `EncounterMasterDaoImpl.java` (the single largest source of findings, 131) is marked peripheral here because it is OPD/encounter data access, not billing calculation, even though its *service interface* is imported by `RazorPaymentController.java` for appointment-confirmation purposes.
- **The parser is structural, not control-flow-aware**, identical caveat to the Billing audit: a catch block containing `throw` anywhere in its body is treated as "properly rethrows" and excluded, even if a nested conditional path could still silently fall through without throwing. Spot-checked (2 samples) — both were direct, unconditional rethrows — but not exhaustively verified across all 1,456 excluded blocks.
- **`status-masks-failure`** is reserved for catches that `return null;` — the exact BR-003/BR-005 pattern already fixed once in `GlobalExceptionHandler.java` (Spring turns a null return into an empty HTTP 200, i.e. failure looks like success).
- **`silent-swallow`** includes fully empty catch blocks (7,542 of the 8,671 silent-swallow findings) and the common pattern of returning a generic/hardcoded error response without ever referencing the caught exception variable in the body — a correctly-flagged error status reaches the caller, but the real exception is never logged or referenced anywhere, so the actual cause is unrecoverable in production. The per-row Notes column says explicitly which sub-case applies.
- **`other`** is almost entirely `e.printStackTrace()`-only catches: visible on a console/stdout if anyone is watching it live, but not written to any persistent/centralized log, so effectively silent in a deployed environment.
- **Multi-catch clauses** (`catch (TypeA | TypeB e)`) are recorded once, under the last-listed type in the clause, as a parsing simplification — this undercounts distinct exception *types* seen but not the number of catch blocks/findings themselves.
- This audit does **not** re-scan `legacy/Billing` (already fully catalogued in `docs/AUDIT_Billing_exceptions.md`, 767 findings) or any other module — it is Global-only, matching this task's scope.
